question: Postpartum blues (baby blues) typically resolve spontaneously within the first 2 weeks after delivery and do not require pharmacological treatment.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. Postpartum blues are transient, self-limiting, and do not warrant pharmacological treatment. They must be distinguished from postpartum depression (persists beyond 2 weeks, impairs function) which does require treatment.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Postpartum blues occur in 50–80% of women, peak around days 3–5, and resolve by day 10–14. They are a normal physiological response to rapid hormonal shifts (oestrogen/progesterone withdrawal). Reassurance, rest, and social support are sufficient — no antidepressants are indicated.
